content.user_title: Build SSR-Safe Markstream Views in Nuxt
content.value_statement: Nuxt applications can fail during SSR when browser-only rendering tools load on the server. This skill guides safe markstream-vue setup, mode selection, streaming behavior, and MarkdownRender integration.
actual_capabilities: Confirms whether a repository uses Nuxt 3 or Nuxt 4.
Recommends client-only boundaries for browser-dependent peers.
Selects chat, docs, or minimal renderer modes by UI surface.
Configures streaming and recovered chat history without hydration mismatches.
Preserves safe HTML and Mermaid defaults for untrusted content.
limitations: It does not install packages or run commands without your approval.
It only covers markstream-vue integration in Nuxt 3 and Nuxt 4.
It cannot prove a custom peer dependency is SSR-safe.
Trusted HTML settings require your own security review.

use_cases.title: Add a chat renderer
use_cases.description: Create an SSR-safe streaming chat view with the appropriate renderer mode and client boundary.

use_cases.title: Render documentation pages
use_cases.description: Configure rich document rendering while keeping browser-only peers out of server execution.

use_cases.title: Fix hydration issues
use_cases.description: Review first-screen streaming settings that can cause Nuxt hydration mismatches or blank flashes.

prompt_templates.title: Start a basic integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Add markstream-vue to this Nuxt 3 page. Keep the setup SSR-safe and explain each required file change.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a renderer mode
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Nuxt component and choose chat, docs, or minimal mode for MarkdownRender. Explain the choice.

prompt_templates.title: Configure streaming chat
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement a streaming chat response in Nuxt using markstream-vue. Avoid first-screen SSR hydration mismatches.

prompt_templates.title: Review trusted content
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this client-only MarkdownRender surface. Keep safe HTML and Mermaid settings unless trusted content is documented.

output_examples.input: Add a streaming assistant response to a Nuxt chat page.
output: Use chat mode for the live response.
Keep smooth streaming in auto mode for SSR safety.
Use a client-only boundary for browser-dependent peers.

output_examples.input: Render saved chat messages after a page reload.
output: Keep chat mode on the existing chat row.
Disable smooth streaming for completed history.
Enable fade only when a history-entry animation is required.

output_examples.input: Enable older trusted HTML behavior in one view.
output: Limit the change to a documented client-only surface.
Use trusted HTML only after reviewing the content source.
Keep strict Mermaid behavior unless a justified exception exists.

best_practices: Use client-only wrappers or client plugins for browser-dependent peers.
Keep smooth streaming in auto mode for first-screen SSR content.
Use safe HTML and strict Mermaid settings unless content trust is documented.
anti_patterns: Do not access browser globals during server-side module initialization.
Do not enable smooth streaming on first-screen SSR content.
Do not enable trusted HTML for content from unreviewed sources.

faq.question: Which Nuxt versions does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports Nuxt 3 and Nuxt 4 integration guidance.

faq.question: Which renderer mode should I use for chat?
faq.answer: Use chat mode for AI chat and server-sent event output.

faq.question: How should I load the stylesheet?
faq.answer: Import a markstream-vue stylesheet from a client-safe application shell or plugin.

faq.question: Can I use Monaco or Mermaid during SSR?
faq.answer: Treat these heavy browser-dependent peers as client-only unless your project has a proven SSR pattern.

faq.question: Why should smooth streaming use auto mode?
faq.answer: Auto mode waits for mount and helps prevent first-screen hydration mismatches.

faq.question: When can I use trusted HTML?
faq.answer: Use it only for a documented trusted client-only surface after reviewing the content source.
